claims.note: Only the abstract was read, so no value is confirmed. What the abstract says: fish acclimated at 20 °C to long days (L:D 16:8) had an incipient upper lethal temperature of 29.9 °C, and to short days (8:16) 28.8 °C; long-day fish also resisted longer at all but one test temperature. If the full text agrees, the paper should give the condition: 'at 20 °C acclimation (28.8 °C on short days, 29.9 °C on long days)' — a UILT depends on the acclimation temperature, and Hot Brook's summer water is warmer than 20 °C. species3.js's 'the least heat-tolerant of the four' is a comparison the abstract does not make.
